Carries the three standing claim blockers recorded at the top level of this manifest. Digest-bound so the disclosure cannot drift away from the bytes it describes.

capacity_workload.name: mps_capacity_131072_sites_bond768_v1
capacity_workload.premise_established_note: No measured MPS shape is recorded as release-grade evidence that both exhausts one A800 and completes sharded at the same configuration, so the premise is unestablished and the gate must report it. What is on record is a development-smoke pair at one shape, 131,072 sites and bond dimension 768 at batch size one: a single-device CUDA out-of-memory record (benchmarks/results/local/mps_capacity_131072q_chi768_1xa800_oom_20260805.json, 75,148,300,800 peak bytes against an 85,093,777,408 byte device) and a 16-rank completion over two nodes (benchmarks/results/local/mps_capacity_131072q_chi768_16xa800_repeat_complete_20260806.json, world_size 16, local_world_size 8, node_count 2). Both records share the topology fingerprint c74a91e3a224a4dd414cfbfbcb31da7570880d42e6aa4eaccecf4b85427940a5, and both are development smoke: benchmark_evidence_class is local_non_release, claim_evidence_type is development_smoke, scalability_claim_allowed and release_gate_allowed are false on both, the single-device record carries no commit field, and neither carries a signed measured_production_run envelope, so neither is a premise this contract may build a release claim on. The completion record's single_gpu_capacity_failure flag is inherited from the failure record rather than re-measured in the same signed run. The premise becomes established only by sealing a signed single_gpu_capacity_failure artifact and a signed multi_gpu_capacity_completion artifact at this frozen workload's digest, which is what the release gate requires.

premise_provenance.note: The only recorded multi-node MPS capacity completion was measured in a checkout whose revision is not in this repository's history, so its recorded commit cannot be resolved here, and it recorded a workload-body digest that differs from the body on disk. Two of its five sources, the raw log and the device telemetry, are absent. The premise producer therefore accepts the failure record it names, because that record and its digest are present and verified, and reports the rest as unverifiable rather than implying that it re-verified them. This drift is why the premise cannot be promoted on the strength of this artifact, and why a release run re-measures both legs at the digests frozen here.

capacity_workload.reverse_checkpoint_budget_note: The reverse tape is bounded at the frozen formula's value for the world size that ran, because the bound changes a rank's memory profile and not the arithmetic. Every measurement records the value it ran under, so a reader can tell whether a rank completed because the device holds the workload or because the tape was bounded.

single_gpu_baseline.rationale: One device has no ranks to shard one logical MPS across: its site ownership map is the whole state on one rank, so a world_size 1 artifact can never be a release payload and is read only as the provenance that shows the frozen workload exceeds one device. The strict promotion audit requires every file under benchmarks/results/scalability to be release-grade sharded scalability evidence, so the sealed baseline is written to its own candidate directory and is never promoted. The directory named here is where the capacity-failure role writes that sealed baseline; it currently holds nothing, and the only MPS single-device exhaustion measured so far is the development-smoke record digest-bound under frozen_evidence, which is not release-grade and cannot be read as the baseline.

workload_definition_sources.role: workload body: site count, bond schedule, rank boundary set and the circuit the capacity step trains

capacity_workload.workload_definition_sources_note: The launcher pins the site count and the body builds the circuit, so both files define the frozen workload and both digests are checked. Digesting only the launcher would let the work the contract claims to have measured change under a stable filename.
capacity_workload.workload_limitations: The frozen workload parameterizes a small number of shared scalar angles on 17 wires of a 131,072-site MPS and trains one Adam step against a single-site Z observable. It is a systems workload: it measures whether one logical MPS state can be held and updated across ranks, and it is not an application-quality or expressivity claim. The probe blocker toy_circuit_parameters_only is a standing statement about this kind of parameterization and is disclosed, not retired, here.
capacity_workload.workload_sha256_note: The digest every capacity artifact must carry as workload_sha256. It is the digest of the frozen workload definition named by workload_definition_path, because that file is what fixes the site count, the bond dimension and the rank boundaries a completion artifact is compared against.

freeze_note: This contract was frozen before any MPS release run exists. It freezes the capacity workload (131,072 sites, maximum bond dimension 768, batch size one, one Adam step, approximate two-site gradient), the release topology (16 ranks over two hosts of eight devices each, which is the cluster that exists and the only sharded MPS configuration measured), the per-rank and MPS-specific artifact field contract, and the matched-speed acceptance thresholds. It deliberately freezes no matched-speed configuration ladder and no measured single-device speed floor, because no MPS matched-speed measurement of any kind has been taken: choosing timed configurations before a single MPS timing exists would freeze a protocol whose feasibility is unknown, which is how the tensor-network ladder came to contain an acceptance configuration that cannot run. The contract also records capacity_workload.premise_established=false: the only MPS single-device exhaustion and the only MPS sharded completion on record are development smoke (see capacity_workload.premise_established_note), so the release contract has no measured premise yet and the gate must report the missing premise rather than assume one. Every measured artifact this contract rests on is digest-bound under capacity_workload.frozen_evidence.

release_payload_envelope.note: The frozen MPS release world is 16 ranks, eight devices on each of two hosts, but every scope the evidence envelope defines carries at most eight devices, and the envelope enforces that bound both when a payload is sealed and when it is verified. No signed measured_production_run artifact can therefore describe this release world today: the sealer refuses a 16-device provenance record and the verifier rejects one, so the contract can be evaluated but not satisfied. The gate reports release_world_size_not_carriable_by_evidence_envelope rather than a missing artifact, because the missing thing is a capability of the envelope and not of the run. Widening the scope vocabulary is owned by flagquantum/runtime/observability/evidence.py, which this contract does not modify: a 16-device scope is a change to a shared release-evidence surface, so it lands as its own integration change with its own tests. The bound is stated here as three lists of numbers rather than derived at read time because a manifest is a frozen document; the gate derives the same bound by asking the envelope, and a disagreement means this note must be re-frozen.

runtime.accepted_backward_execution_statuses_not: The reverse-pass statuses the producer emits for a measured backward pass. The gate matches this list exactly rather than searching the label for 'executed' or 'production', because a projected or simulated reverse pass can name itself in the vocabulary of a measurement.
runtime.fallback_semantics_note: The single fallback declaration a release payload may carry. MPS training is approximate, so a payload that recomputed the same workload through a statevector path, a replicated per-rank autograd replay, or one rank holding a full local MPS would report numbers that are not sharded MPS evidence. The gate requires this exact string and an empty fallback_events list, because the sealed envelope records the fallback events the run observed.
runtime.launcher_note: The launcher is torchrun with one process per device, and it owns the process-group rendezvous: the executor does not initialize the group, so a rank that cannot reach its peers fails visibly instead of silently re-running the workload locally.

speed_workload.name: mps_matched_speed_v1
speed_workload.thresholds_note: Every number in this block is an acceptance threshold to be crossed, not a measurement. No MPS matched-speed measurement of any kind exists: there is no measured single-device leg at any configuration and no measured sharded leg, which is why measured_single_device_floor is empty rather than populated with the capacity workload's numbers, which were measured for capacity and not for speed. The configuration ladder is deliberately unfrozen (configuration_ladder is null) because no MPS configuration has been chosen or measured for timing, so there is nothing to choose it from; a later revision must freeze the ladder before any timed run, and until then the gate reports speed_configuration_ladder_not_frozen alongside the missing speed artifact. The thresholds themselves are protocol: they are the levels a future speed comparison must reach to be accepted, and they are fixed here so that they are not chosen after the numbers are known.
speed_workload.timing_unit: one full forward-and-reverse sharded MPS training step, measured end to end on the ranks it is sharded across

standing_blockers.name: host_staging_in_measured_region
standing_blockers.statement: The two-node transport probe staged ranks through host memory inside the measured region, so its timing is not device-to-device transport. A later transfer measurement can retire this blocker.

standing_blockers.name: toy_circuit_parameters_only
standing_blockers.statement: The probe exercised a toy parameterization rather than an application circuit. No measurement of this probe retires the statement, so it is recorded as a standing limitation of the transport evidence rather than as an outstanding task.

standing_blockers.name: two_node_pair_only_no_wider_topology
standing_blockers.statement: Only one pair of hosts exists here, so no measurement on this cluster can widen the topology. This is disclosed as a permanent boundary of the capability, not as a stage of its measurement, and it matches the frozen release topology of two nodes.

topologies.note: The measured cluster is one pair of hosts with eight A800 devices each, so the release topology is 16 ranks: eight per host, one rank per device, distributed across both hosts. The frozen capacity workload fixes its 15 rank boundaries for that world size, so a different world size computes a different boundary set and a different topology fingerprint. No third host exists here, which is why the frozen topology is a pair of hosts rather than a ladder, and why the pair-only boundary is disclosed as a permanent limitation of the capability rather than as a stage of its measurement.
